focus_areas.label: Gardenly Mern Stack Performance And Infrastructure
focus_areas.anchor_context: Full-stack garden management app claiming 78% API latency reduction (252ms to 54ms) via Redis caching and Apache Solr, containerized with Docker and CI/CD.

Apache Solr integration alongside MongoDB IXSCAN indexing
Docker containerization and GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline
Redux state management across 5 user roles
resume_snippets: Boosted API performance by ~78% (252ms → 54ms) via Redis caching and Apache Solr enterprise search, with MongoDB IXSCAN indexing across 5 collections
Built a full-stack MERN application with 13 RESTful API modules, 5 user roles, Redux state management, JWT + Google OAuth 2.0 authentication, and real-time Socket.IO community feed
focus_areas.why_priority: The 78% latency claim is highly specific and defensible — forces the candidate to explain exactly what was cached, how i
focus_areas.opener: You measured 252ms to 54ms on Gardenly — before I accept that number, tell me: was that median latency, p95, or a single hot-path request, and what load was on the system when you took the baseline?

dimensions.label: Redis Caching Strategy and Cache Invalidation
dimensions.resume_anchor: Boosted API performance by ~78% (252ms → 54ms) via Redis caching and Apache Solr enterprise search, with MongoDB IXSCAN indexing across 5 collections
dimensions.surface: Across your 13 API modules in Gardenly, which specific routes did you put behind Redis caching, and what TTL did you assign them?
dimensions.mechanism: With 5 user roles in Gardenly each seeing different data, how did your Redis key structure prevent one role's cached response from being served to another?
dimensions.boundary: When a garden resource was updated by one of your 5 roles, which cache keys needed invalidation, and how did your invalidation logic know which ones to target without flushing everything?

dimensions.label: Apache Solr Integration and MongoDB IXSCAN Indexing
dimensions.resume_anchor: Boosted API performance by ~78% (252ms → 54ms) via Redis caching and Apache Solr enterprise search, with MongoDB IXSCAN indexing across 5 collections
dimensions.surface: In Gardenly, which queries were routed to Apache Solr versus hitting MongoDB directly, and what was the deciding factor?
dimensions.mechanism: MongoDB IXSCAN across 5 collections implies compound or covered indexes — for one of those collections, what fields were in the index and what query pattern made that index necessary?
dimensions.boundary: When data was written to MongoDB in Gardenly, how did Solr's index stay consistent with it — what mechanism synchronized the two, and what happened to search results during the lag window?

dimensions.label: Docker Containerization and GitHub Actions CI/CD
dimensions.resume_anchor: Containerized with Docker, automated via GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline, and shipped with Swagger API documentation and Jest-based test coverage across 5 controller test suites
dimensions.surface: In your Gardenly Docker setup, how many containers were in your compose configuration, and what service did each one run?
dimensions.mechanism: Your GitHub Actions pipeline ran Jest across 5 controller test suites — at what stage did tests run relative to the Docker build, and what caused a pipeline failure to block a deploy?
dimensions.boundary: In your GitHub Actions pipeline, which Jest suite was most likely to produce a false-green — one that passed in CI but would break in production — and what in your test isolation caused that gap?

dimensions.label: Socket.IO Real-Time Community Feed Architecture
dimensions.resume_anchor: Built a full-stack MERN application with 13 RESTful API modules, 5 user roles, Redux state management, JWT + Google OAuth 2.0 authentication, and real-time Socket.IO community feed
dimensions.surface: In Gardenly's Socket.IO community feed, how did you scope which users received a given event — broadcast to all connections or targeted by room or namespace?
dimensions.mechanism: With JWT authentication also present in Gardenly, how did you verify a user's identity and role on an incoming Socket.IO connection before allowing them to join a feed channel?
dimensions.boundary: If a user's session expired mid-connection on the Socket.IO feed, what happened to their socket — did your server detect the stale JWT, and how did you handle the disconnect or re-auth without losing their feed state?

dimensions.label: Redux State Management Across 5 User Roles
dimensions.resume_anchor: Built a full-stack MERN application with 13 RESTful API modules, 5 user roles, Redux state management, JWT + Google OAuth 2.0 authentication, and real-time Socket.IO community feed
dimensions.surface: In Gardenly's Redux store, how did you structure state slices to accommodate the 5 different user roles — one shared store or role-segmented slices?
dimensions.mechanism: When a user with one role performed an action that updated shared data in Gardenly, how did your Redux store ensure other components tied to a different role's view reflected that change correctly?
dimensions.boundary: Google OAuth 2.0 and JWT are both present in Gardenly — when the OAuth token arrived on the client, how did it flow into Redux state, and what Redux slice or middleware owned the decision of which role to assign that session?

dimensions.label: Dual-Layer Authentication: JWT and Clerk
